claims.text: Conventional preparation of single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 exhibits significant porosity.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 exhibits grain growth that compromises strength.
Porosity and grain growth promote defect formation under liquid-plating conditions.
SPS can consolidate single-phase ZrB2 below 2300 °C.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will be denser than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will have finer grains than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will contain fewer processing defects than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Pulsed electric current during SPS accelerates mass transport.
Accelerated mass transport during SPS promotes rapid densification at lower temperatures.
Rapid SPS densification inhibits excessive grain growth and pore formation.
A denser, finer-grained ZrB2 microstructure is less prone to hole formation during liquid-plating-bath exposure.
Reduced hole formation will enhance the mechanical integrity of ZrB2 during prolonged liquid-plating-bath exposure.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will have greater mechanical strength than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will retain more mechanical strength after liquid-plating-bath exposure than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will develop fewer and smaller holes during long-duration liquid-plating-bath exposure.
The experiment will compare conventionally sintered and SPS-prepared ZrB2 made from identical starting powders and exposed to identical bath conditions.
Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in porosity and hole formation together with improved post-exposure strength retention will falsify the hypothesis.
